# MeedyaDL 1.4.4

A maintenance-and-UX release: music videos download more reliably, the queue is faster and reorderable, Explicit albums with multiple audio qualities no longer split into duplicate folders, and background processing after a download finishes is significantly faster.

### What's new

- **Reorder downloads in the queue.** Right-click any queued item to move it to the top, up, down, or to the bottom — even while other downloads are running. The order survives an app restart.
- **Real music-video titles in the Activity log**, instead of a generic "unknown" placeholder.
- **iTunes Store links now work automatically.** Pasting an `itunes.apple.com` link downloads correctly instead of silently failing — MeedyaDL now converts it to the equivalent Apple Music link behind the scenes.
- **Live progress for audio fingerprinting and loudness analysis.** The per-item progress bar now shows exactly which track is being processed instead of sitting on a static label for a minute or more on heavy albums.

### What's fixed

- **Explicit albums with multiple audio qualities enabled (for example, a Dolby Atmos download with an automatic Lossless copy) no longer split into two separate folders on disk.** Both qualities now land together in the same album folder, the way you'd expect.
- **Large, "heavy" albums (long track counts, multiple audio-quality tiers, or several music videos) no longer trigger a false "some files may be missing tags" warning** — MeedyaDL now gives itself enough time based on the actual size of the job instead of a one-size-fits-all timer.
- **MeedyaDL no longer wastes several minutes retrying a known Apple Music-side music-video artwork bug.** It now reports the failure once instead of retrying with no chance of success.
- **Music-video companion downloads no longer claim success when nothing actually downloaded** — the Activity log now accurately reports when zero videos were produced.

### Performance

- **Finishing touches after a download completes (audio fingerprinting, loudness analysis, and related lookups) are roughly 40–50% faster on heavy albums** — around 210 seconds down to about 120 seconds on a 19-track live album with every optional feature turned on. These steps now run fully in parallel instead of partly one-after-another.
- **The queue stays smooth with a large number of items.** Only the rows currently on screen are rendered, and a single download's progress update no longer causes every other row in the list to redraw. Most noticeable with 50+ queued items, dramatic with 500+.
